page: Microsoft Azure E8pds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Epdsv6 server family. It is powered by an ARM-based Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor featuring 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs running at 3.4 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Additionally, the server is equipped with 472 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong memory subsystem performance, with the Passmark memory score ranking in the top tier (top 10%). Single-threaded gzip compression performance is also strong, placing in the top 25%. Most other compute and memory bandwidth metrics, including stress-ng CPU performance, bzip3 decompression, and Redis SET operations, fall within the average range. However, the system exhibits weaker performance in specific areas, such as the Passmark CPU encryption test and prompt processing for medium-sized large language models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E8pds_v6 offers a highly dense memory profile relative to its vCPU count, making it a viable option for memory-bound workloads without the overhead of higher-tier compute resources. The combination of dedicated ARM cores, 64.0 GB of RAM, and 472 GB of local storage makes this server well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, web serving, and general-purpose data processing tasks that benefit from high memory-to-core ratios.
description: Microsoft Azure E8pds_v6 is an ARM-based, memory-optimized virtual machine from the Epdsv6 family, running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 8 dedicated physical cores powered by a 3.4 GHz Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor, paired with 64.0 GB of RAM and 472 GB of local storage. The server delivers a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU, with benchmark results highlighting top-tier memory performance in the top 10% and strong single-threaded gzip compression. While cryptographic and certain LLM inference tasks show weaker relative performance, its overall profile offers excellent qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive applications. The E8pds_v6 is highly suited for database operations, caching layers, and memory-bound enterprise workloads.
